causal_hypothesis: The prior GraphQL HTTP 500 is caused by the pinned SGLang image or large bootstrap payload rather than inability of RunPod's shared deployment backend to create any advertised AP-IN-1 H100 Pod.

candidate_change.from: pinned SGLang digest plus bootstrap environment, command, and artifact port
candidate_change.to: standard runpod/pytorch image with 20 GB container disk, 20 GB volume, and no custom env, command, or ports

workload_geometry.post_create_action: one allowlisted REST state read followed immediately by deletion

requirements: GraphQL response contains pod id and positive hourly price

telemetry.missing_runtime_metrics_interpretation: not an inference or utilization result

kill_conditions: any Pod ID triggers unconditional deletion

next_step_rules.on_control_pass: Decompose the pinned image and bootstrap payload with the cheapest single-variable GraphQL follow-up.
next_step_rules.on_control_preallocation_failure: Classify the direct Pod create backend as unavailable for this account/placement and pivot to a different in-scope provider or managed API evidence path.
next_step_rules.on_cleanup_failure: Continue deletion attempts and do not run another allocation until 404 is verified.

claim_boundary: This control can establish only whether minimal H100 Pod placement works. It provides no model, quality, latency, throughput, utilization, power, or cost-per-token evidence.
